what: Otis makes, installs, services and modernises elevators and escalators in more than 200 countries. The service contracts on roughly two million units already installed are where almost all of its profit comes from.
customers: Building owners and managers, construction contractors and developers worldwide.
money: maintenance contracts, repairs and modernisation of installed units
the larger part of revenue, thin margin
moat: Two million elevators already installed, each needing regulated inspection and maintenance for decades, which almost always goes to the manufacturer.
risks: Chinese new building has collapsed, and China was its largest new equipment market
Revenue grew only about 1% last year
Debt of about $9 billion against under $1 billion of cash
Independent service providers compete for maintenance contracts
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 55%, among the highest of any large industrial company
Modernising ageing elevators in Europe and North America is a growing, high-margin market
Service revenue grows with the installed base regardless of new construction
watch: Service portfolio growth and new equipment orders, especially in China.
